technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment within the existing Spring-based Java codebase using Java 17-compatible APIs and preserving existing public behavior by retaining backward-compatible defaults.
Expose CodeGen Options and Merge Options through the existing job, processor, or configuration model rather than introducing a separate configuration subsystem.

Implement timeout as a configurable execution deadline with a default that preserves current behavior; ensure timeout termination and failure status are propagated through the existing job execution path.
Support SQL statements and scripts through a dedicated processor or job statement abstraction, using the existing JDBC/data-source infrastructure and parameter binding where available.
Add an injectable RowMapper<Tuple> extension point to the JDBC reader/factory so users can enrich tuples without recreating immutable tuples in a downstream processor.
Implement expressions using the framework's existing expression language mechanism where possible, with controlled evaluation context and expression support in file and directory naming properties.
Implement configurable delimiter escaping in the CSV/output serialization path, preserving the current output behavior when escaping is disabled or unspecified.
Refactor MessageBus message transformation around a low-allocation transformation interface and avoid unnecessary intermediate message objects, while preserving message semantics and compatibility.
Use unit tests for component behavior and integration tests for end-to-end job, JDBC, filesystem, timeout, and MessageBus scenarios.
assumptions: The estimate covers implementation, automated tests, integration validation, and documentation for all eight user stories in one existing repository.
The existing build, CI pipeline, test framework, job model, JDBC support, tuple model, output writers, and MessageBus are available and functional.
No database schema migration, external service development, or changes to Spring Framework itself are required.
Existing configuration formats and APIs can be extended without a major version migration; compatibility defaults will be maintained.
SQL execution is limited to the existing configured data sources and does not require a new transaction-management model.
Expression support is limited to configured naming and path-related properties and does not require arbitrary code execution.
Delimiter escaping targets the existing delimited-text/CSV output implementation and supports the escaping rules required by the current Hive/HAWQ use case.
Performance validation for the MessageBus refactor uses representative benchmarks and regression tests rather than a full production-scale performance qualification.
One workday represents approximately eight hours of focused development effort by one developer; estimates exclude elapsed waiting time and external review delays.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing job, processor, JDBC reader, tuple, output, configuration, timeout, and MessageBus implementations; identify extension points, compatibility constraints, and detailed implementation design for the eight stories.
Add configuration properties and runtime propagation for CodeGen Options, including validation, default handling, wiring into code-generation execution, and backward-compatible behavior.
Add configurable Merge Options, propagate them through the job and megastore-related execution path, validate values, and preserve existing merge behavior when options are omitted.
Add timeout configuration, enforce it around the relevant job or processor execution, handle cancellation and hung execution, and expose an appropriate failure result and diagnostic logging.

activities.activity_name: Add SQL statement and script execution
activities.activity_description: Implement processor/job support for executing SQL statements and scripts through the existing JDBC infrastructure, including parameter handling, transaction/error behavior, and result reporting.

Introduce an injectable RowMapper<Tuple> extension point in the JDBC reader or ItemReaderFactory path, wire custom mapping into tuple creation, and retain the default mapper behavior for existing users.
Enable expressions in configured directory and file naming properties, provide the required evaluation context for timestamps and intermediate data, and add validation and safe failure behavior.
Extend delimited output serialization with configurable escaping and quoting behavior for delimiter characters, including compatibility defaults and handling of related special characters.

Refactor the programmatic MessageBus message transformation path to reduce allocations and transformation overhead, preserve ordering and message semantics, and add focused throughput regression coverage.

Create and execute tests covering configuration binding, defaults, SQL execution, custom row mapping, expressions, escaping, timeout behavior, MessageBus semantics, and representative end-to-end job flows; fix defects found during testing.
Document new configuration options and extension points, add representative examples, update compatibility notes, perform final build and CI validation, and prepare the increment for delivery.
